concepts.name: Three telemetry signals
concepts.summary: Name metrics, logs and traces and state what kind of information each one provides.

concepts.name: Monitoring versus observability
concepts.summary: Explain that monitoring watches for known failure conditions while observability lets you ask new questions about system behaviour from its outputs.

concepts.name: Metrics and time series
concepts.summary: Describe a metric as a numeric measurement sampled over time, such as CPU use, request count or error rate.

concepts.name: Log entries and levels
concepts.summary: Read a log line, identify its timestamp, severity level and message, and explain what each level is for.

concepts.name: Health checks and uptime
concepts.summary: Explain how a simple health check or ping reports whether a service is up and what it cannot tell you.

concepts.name: Dashboards and alerts purpose
concepts.summary: Distinguish a dashboard for human exploration from an alert that notifies someone when action is needed.

concepts.name: Host resource metrics
concepts.summary: Interpret basic CPU, memory, disk and network usage figures for a machine and recognise saturation.

misconceptions.text: Observability is just another word for monitoring dashboards.
If the health check passes, users must be having a good experience.
High CPU usage always means something is broken.

concepts.name: Metric types
concepts.summary: Choose between counter, gauge and histogram for a given measurement and use each correctly.

concepts.name: Metric labels and cardinality
concepts.summary: Add labels to metrics to slice data by dimension while avoiding labels with unbounded values.

concepts.name: Structured logging
concepts.summary: Emit logs as structured key-value fields so they can be filtered and searched by machine.

concepts.name: Basic instrumentation with a library
concepts.summary: Add counters, gauges and timers to application code and expose them for collection.

concepts.name: Scrape versus push collection
concepts.summary: Explain how a collector pulls metrics from endpoints versus applications pushing data, and when each fits.

concepts.name: Rates and percentiles
concepts.summary: Compute and read request rates and latency percentiles rather than relying on raw counter values or averages.

concepts.name: Threshold alert rules
concepts.summary: Write a simple alert rule with a threshold and duration that fires on a clear symptom.

concepts.name: Log search and filtering
concepts.summary: Find relevant entries in centralised logs using time ranges, fields and text filters.

misconceptions.text: Average latency is enough to describe how fast a service is for users.
Adding more labels to a metric is free and always makes it more useful.
A counter's raw value is meaningful on its own, rather than its rate of change.

concepts.name: Distributed tracing spans
concepts.summary: Instrument a request path so that spans with parent-child relationships form a trace across services.

concepts.name: Context propagation and correlation IDs
concepts.summary: Pass trace or request identifiers across service boundaries and into logs to link signals for one request.

concepts.name: Golden signals and RED/USE
concepts.summary: Select latency, traffic, errors and saturation, or RED and USE, to structure what to measure for a service or resource.

concepts.name: Service level indicators and objectives
concepts.summary: Define an SLI from user-facing behaviour and set an SLO target, analysing what it implies for reliability.

concepts.name: Dashboard design
concepts.summary: Analyse and organise dashboards so that panels answer specific questions and reveal problems quickly.

concepts.name: Actionable alerting
concepts.summary: Distinguish alerts that need human action from noise, and favour symptom-based alerts over cause-based ones.

concepts.name: Incident triage with telemetry
concepts.summary: Move from an alert to a narrowed cause by correlating metrics, logs and traces systematically.

concepts.name: Log aggregation pipelines
concepts.summary: Set up agents and pipelines that collect, parse, enrich and store logs from many hosts.

misconceptions.text: Alert on every metric that could indicate a problem so nothing is missed.
An SLO of 100% is the right goal for a reliable service.
Traces replace the need for logs and metrics.

concepts.name: Error budgets and burn rate alerts
concepts.summary: Evaluate alerting based on error budget consumption speed and choose windows that balance speed and precision.

concepts.name: Cardinality and cost management
concepts.summary: Assess the storage and query cost of telemetry and decide what to drop, aggregate or keep.

concepts.name: Vendor-neutral instrumentation standards
concepts.summary: Analyse how a common instrumentation API and collector decouple application code from backends.

concepts.name: Sampling strategies for traces
concepts.summary: Compare head and tail sampling and judge which retains the traces needed for diagnosis at acceptable cost.

concepts.name: High-cardinality event analysis
concepts.summary: Use wide, context-rich events to slice by arbitrary dimensions and find unknown-unknown causes.

concepts.name: Alert quality evaluation
concepts.summary: Review alerts by precision, recall, detection time and actionability, and retire or redesign poor ones.

concepts.name: Blameless postmortem analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate incidents to find contributing factors and turn the findings into observability improvements.

concepts.name: Monitoring dependencies and synthetic checks
concepts.summary: Combine black-box probes with internal metrics to detect failures in dependencies and user journeys.

misconceptions.text: Collecting and keeping all telemetry at full fidelity is always the safest approach.
Random head sampling reliably keeps the slow or erroring traces you need.
Postmortems should identify the single person or root cause that failed.

concepts.name: Observability strategy design
concepts.summary: Design an organisation-wide telemetry architecture that balances coverage, cost, latency and ownership.

concepts.name: Scalable telemetry backend architecture
concepts.summary: Evaluate sharding, federation, downsampling and retention designs for metrics, log and trace backends.

concepts.name: Anomaly detection and automated diagnosis
concepts.summary: Judge when statistical or learned detection beats static thresholds and how to limit false positives.

concepts.name: SLO programme and reliability governance
concepts.summary: Create SLO practices and error budget policies that guide product and engineering trade-offs across teams.

concepts.name: Observability of complex failure modes
concepts.summary: Evaluate instrumentation needed to expose cascading failures, retry storms, queueing effects and partial outages.

concepts.name: Observability-driven development
concepts.summary: Create development, release and testing practices that build observability in and use it to verify changes safely.

concepts.name: Telemetry pipeline reliability and security
concepts.summary: Evaluate how to keep telemetry pipelines reliable, independent of the systems they watch, and free of sensitive data.

misconceptions.text: Machine-learning anomaly detection removes the need for well-designed SLO alerts.
Buying a single observability platform solves the observability problem.
The monitoring stack can safely share the same failure domain as the production system.
